data.turoyo: komər mədle u sayfayḏe qṭəʕle qarʕe di ḥayye, w mšatfole w masləqole lalʕal, mšaṭfole ṭrele u qarʕo ʕal xasra, <...>
data.translation: Er nahm sein Schwert und schlug der Schlange den Kopf ab, hackte sie in Stücke und brachte sie nach oben. Er zerstückelte sie, legte aber den Kopf zur Seite, <...>

rationale: Thin II Preterit plus unusual object-bearing forms; one continuous context preserves the adjacent t/ṭ variants.

summary: Both tokens are II Preterit, with feminine object -o before third-person masculine agent -le. The animal patient and cutting sequence support division into pieces, not a new verb sense.
mšatfole and mšaṭfole alternate nonemphatic and emphatic spelling in the same verse. Preserve both; one passage does not establish a dialect contrast by itself.
One added example represents both tokens, leaving two existing-plus-new II Preterit examples in the cell. No new stem, box or fixed idiom is supported.
Is the t/ṭ alternation in JTM 5.3/34 phonetic, editorial, or a transcription inconsistency? No source text is normalized.
A snake as dismembered patient extends the inherited stone-splitting example, within the existing auseinander reissen/spalten meaning.
